issues.legal_issue: A transferee who acquires property from a judgment-debtor after a suit concerning that property has begun cannot resist execution of a decree for possession by claiming through the judgment-debtor.
material_facts: A suit seeking possession of the property was filed against the transferors.
While that suit was pending, the transferors sold their interest in the property to the objector.
A decree for possession was later passed and the decree-holder began execution proceedings.
The objector claimed through the transferors and resisted execution while relying on a separate suit she had filed challenging the decree.
issues.conclusion: The objector was a transferee pendente lite and could not resist or obstruct execution; the separate suit she had filed did not entitle her to protection from execution.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rules 97–103 of the Code of Civil Procedure govern resistance to delivery of possession; Rule 102 excludes a transferee pendente lite from the protections in Rules 98 and 100. This reflects the doctrine of lis pendens in Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. The Court relied on Bellamy v. Sabine, (1857) 1 DG & J 566; Silverline Forum Pvt. Ltd. v. Rajiv Trust, (1998) 3 SCC 723; Sarvinder Singh v. Dalip Singh, (1996) 5 SCC 539; and approved the relevant principle in Vijayalakshmi Leather Industries (P) Ltd. v. K. Narayanan, Lalitha, AIR 2003 Mad 203. The limited inquiry is whether the objector acquired the property during the suit and claims through the judgment-debtor; notice of the litigation is immaterial.

rule.if: possession_decree_execution and transfer_after_suit_filed and claims_through_judgment_debtor and transferee_resists_execution

predicates.possession_decree_execution: A decree-holder is executing a decree for possession of immovable property.
predicates.transfer_after_suit_filed: The judgment-debtor transferred the property after a suit concerning it had been filed.
predicates.claims_through_judgment_debtor: The person resisting execution claims the property through the judgment-debtor.
predicates.transferee_resists_execution: The transferee resists or obstructs delivery of possession in execution.

issues.definition: When a person claims through a judgment-debtor under a transfer made after a suit concerning the property began and resists execution of a possession decree, that person cannot resist execution.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee pendente lite cannot obtain a stay of execution merely because the transferee has filed a separate suit challenging the decree.
material_facts: The property was transferred to the objector while the decree-holder’s suit concerning it was pending.
The objector filed a separate suit challenging the decree and sought to prevent execution until that suit was decided.
The executing court stayed execution, but the High Court set that order aside.
issues.conclusion: The pending suit filed by the transferee did not justify staying execution, and the decree-holder could proceed with execution while that suit remained pending.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure concerns a suit instituted by a judgment-debtor against a decree-holder; it does not apply to a separate suit filed by a third-party transferee pendente lite. Rule 102 of Order XXI and the doctrine of lis pendens under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, prevent such a transferee from using the separate suit to obstruct execution. If the transferee later obtains a decree, the transferee may pursue appropriate proceedings for restitution. The Court relied on Bellamy v. Sabine, (1857) 1 DG & J 566, and Silverline Forum Pvt. Ltd. v. Rajiv Trust, (1998) 3 SCC 723.

rule.if: possession_decree_execution and transfer_after_suit_filed and transferee_filed_separate_challenge_suit and execution_stay_sought

predicates.possession_decree_execution: A decree-holder is executing a decree for possession of immovable property.
predicates.transfer_after_suit_filed: The judgment-debtor transferred the property after a suit concerning it had been filed.
predicates.transferee_filed_separate_challenge_suit: The transferee filed a separate suit challenging the decree or asserting rights in the property.
predicates.execution_stay_sought: The transferee sought to stop execution until the separate suit was decided.

issues.definition: If a transferee acquired the property after the underlying suit began and seeks to halt execution of a possession decree because of a separate challenge suit, execution is not stayed on that basis.
